apps.name: Killer 2s
apps.subtitle: Shed your hand. Save your 2s. Take the pile.
apps.localizedDescription: A shedding card game (Tiến Lên / "Thirteen" / "Killer", with our own ladder, kills and bombs) and a roguelike run on top: crews, tricks, bosses, enhanced cards. Public beta by Devious Developments. Play in landscape.

versions.localizedDescription:
- Decks unlock now: the unlock checks never actually ran. Now they're checked after every table, so a deck unlocks the moment you earn it ("New deck unlocked!" on the table report). Crew and money count at their peak in the run, so holding $50 and then spending it still counts. Your saved progress gets credit where it can prove it: a past win unlocks Pixel, and having cleared circuit 2 unlocks Chalkboard.
- 30 achievements, in a new Achievements tab in the Collection, across plays, runs, money, enhancements, and decks and stakes.
- iPhone: the title screen no longer shows a Quit button. iOS never lets an app close itself; swipe home to leave.

- See every bonus on a card: each enhanced card wears a small chip per bonus down its left edge (gold coin, stone, chrome, holo rainbow, foil swirl, red X for Marked), always visible, even in a fanned hand.
- Hold a card for the details: press and hold a card still (or hover it on PC) and a note above your hand lists each of its bonuses and exactly what it does.

- The iPhone app now says plainly that it never uses the camera, microphone or photos.
- The pause menu re-centres itself if the phone rotates while it's open.

- Fixed: opening the iPhone app switcher froze the game and hid the pause button. Now the pause menu opens when you come back, and a paused game with no menu showing unpauses itself.
- Peek works straight away: use it at the table and the next opponent's whole hand turns face up for the rest of that table (it used to wait for the next table).

- Clear stacking rules: every enhancement trick now says what it is and what it stacks with: a MATERIAL (Gold, Stone), a FINISH (Holo, Chrome, Foil) or a MARK. A card holds one of each.
- Replace warning: using a bonus that would push one off (Holo on a Chrome card) asks first, "Replace with Holo" or "Keep it". The same bonus twice is refused, so you don't waste the trick.
- After a bonus stacks, the table tells you what the card is now ("now Stone + Holo + Marked").

- Enhanced cards shine: every enhancement now has a live, moving finish, with the rank and pips inked on top. Holo is a rainbow film that shifts as you move (Balatro-style), Chrome has mirror bands that sweep across, Foil ripples blue-silver, Gold has a rolling sheen and twinkling glints, and Stone catches the light. On iPhone, tilt the phone and the light moves; on PC, it follows the mouse. Works on every deck.
- Your own sort: Sort now cycles by rank, by suit, and by plays: your hand chained into the fewest plays with the fewest cards left over, laid out singles, pairs, trips, runs, then your 2s.
- Bonuses stack, one of each kind: a card can have a material (Gold or Stone), a finish (Holo, Chrome or Foil) and a Mark, all at once, and each one pays. A new bonus of a kind the card already has replaces the old one.
- Purchase confirmation in the Locker: the first tap on a card for sale selects it and shows what it does; tap it again to buy. Tapping anywhere else cancels.
- The Snitch works: each opponent's highest card shows face-up on their seat, and updates as they play.
- Pause menu: the pause button in the table's top-left corner (or Esc / Start on a controller) stops the table: the CPUs wait, nothing moves. From it: Resume, Sound (volume and mute, remembered), How to play, and Quit run (it asks first) or Main menu at a quick table. On iPhone, leaving the app pauses the table too.
- Peek works: the next opponent's whole hand shows face-up for that table.
- Fixed: after a run, the main menu's deck cards kept that run's enhancements (stone Aces on the deck picker).
- Full Set, tightened: the four have to be played together, one straight after another. If any other play lands in between (say a 5, then a 7, then a pair of 5s), the last 5 is just a 5.

- FULL SET, a new kind of kill: when all four of a card end up on the stack, whoever lays the last of them wins it on the spot, whatever the suits. Got the other two 3s when someone plays a pair of 3s? Drop them: the stack clears, the pile is yours and you lead. A pair onto a single works too. In a run it scores like a KILL.
- Faces at the table: every opponent (and every boss) has a hand-drawn polaroid of their own, taped to their seat, in place of the numbered circle.
- Shop info icons: tap the little ⓘ on any card in the Locker to read what it does, with no more buying by accident.

- New app icon: all four 2s fanned out in your hand, ♠ ♣ ♦ ♥, so every suit shows. On PC (exe, window, browser tab) the background is invisible, just the cards; on iPhone they sit on the studio dark (iOS doesn't allow see-through icons).
- First release to carry the 0.6.1 changes below (0.6.1 itself never went out).

- No more Godot logo anywhere: the iPhone launch screen, the browser loading page and the PC boot all open on the studio dark, straight into our splash.
- The PC exe carries the Killer 2s icon and "Killer 2s · Devious Developments" in its file details.
- The title screen shows the new tagline: Shed your hand. Save your 2s. Take the pile.

- New name: Killer 2s (was "Kill: TCG"). Tagline: Shed your hand. Save your 2s. Take the pile.
- Studio splash: the Devious Developments logo, then the title written on notebook paper. No more Godot stand-ins on boot.
- App icon: the 2♥ on green felt (window, browser tab, iPhone).
- iPhone build (this page) — sideload with Sideloadly or AltStore.
- It's all Kills and Bombs: "chop" is gone; a bomb on 2s is a BOMB.
- The top AI level is now Kingpin.

- Landscape on phones: a phone held upright shows "turn your phone sideways"; Android locks landscape in fullscreen.
- The Table Card (right-hand panel) fills the whole column.
- Tap/click the Table Report to finish the handwriting instantly.
- Enhanced cards stand out: a thick rim in the material's colour + a sticker badge.
- The Locker's focus ring hugs the button (it was enormous).
- Table numbers read per circuit — "1 / 3", "2 / 3", "BOSS" (they showed 4/3, 6/3).
- Table Report: "RESULT" stamp box; "Paid out … (the House)".

- Table Card: the run's side panel is a photocopied form — score, this play (points × cards), crew and tricks taped in.
- Collection: found items taped in; tricks, bosses, decks and enhancements on single lines.
- Enhancement textures: Holographic shimmers, Stone is granite, Chrome, Foil, Gold leaf, Marked — on cards and tiles.
- Bombs play on any stack, like kills; only a bigger bomb beats a bomb.
- Fixed: a card that could stand in a run was greyed out (any suit works in a run).
- Circuit map path no longer runs behind the names. How to Play rewritten (two pages).
- Renamed the opponent "Tardy Tom" → "Snooze Button Sid".

- Table Report and The Locker are photocopied forms: blanks filled in by pen, the maths written out, items taped in.
- Drag cards onto the pile to play (green = legal, red snaps back).
- Locker hover text fixed; the title menu fits on every screen.

- New hand order: single < pair < run of 3 < suited run of 3 < three of a kind < run of 4 < suited run of 4 < … < 2s.
- The round ends the moment you go out — your sweep is one big total.
- Crew (was "Accomplices"): 32 hand-drawn crew cards. Text sits on the notebook lines.

- Scoring = points × cards: every play, every pile you take, and the sweep of every card left when you go out first.
- Runs start one-on-one, then 1 vs 2, then the full table.
- Opponents have names; every venue has its own table cloth.
- Bomb ladder: four of a kind < 3 pairs < 3 triples < 4 pairs < 4 triples < 5 pairs.
- Mixed-suit straights fixed; drag to sort; shortcut letters in the buttons; plays stay on the pile until it clears.
- Scaling crew multiply your score all run — the shop matters. Version shown on the title.

- Rules adopted from Tiến Lên, with our own extended plays (a higher play beats any lower one) and 2s kill.
- Web + phone layouts, controller support, eight deck arts, a calmer Notebook card back.
- The first builds: rules engine, six AI levels, the roguelike run (circuits, bosses, the Locker), deck arts.
